chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ja'far ibn Sama'a, from more than one person, from Aban, from Zurara ibn A'yan who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is the right of Allah upon the servants?' He said: 'That they should say what they know, and refrain from speaking about what they do not know.'

key_terms.الْعِبَاد: The servants — all human beings in their capacity as God's creatures
key_terms.حَقُّ اللَّهِ: The right of Allah — what is due to God from creation; a fundamental obligation
key_terms.يَقِفُوا: They refrain/pause — to restrain oneself from proceeding without knowledge

ai.seo_question: What is the right of Allah upon His servants according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan, one of the foremost companions of Imam al-Baqir (AS), asked the Imam about the fundamental duty of servants towards God. The Imam's answer is succinct and profound: the right of God upon humanity is to speak only from knowledge and to remain silent on that which is unknown. This teaching directly addresses the prohibition of speaking about religious matters without knowledge, a foundational principle in Islamic epistemology that distinguishes authentic religious guidance from speculation.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Zurara Bin Ayn who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is a Right of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon the servants?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That he should be saying what he knows, and refraining during what he does not know’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ja’far ibn Sama‘a from several persons, from aban, from Zurara ibn A‘yan who has said the following. “I asked Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.) this, ‘What are the rights of Allah on people?’”
The Imam (a.s.) replied, “They must say what they know and abstain from saying anything that they have no knowledge of.’”
